In the game

Selsior is in the game today. See Selsior in the world guide for its maps, NPCs and shops.

Design notes

Classic medieval fantasy architecture. Joyful, bustling and cosmopolitan. New with this page: the Treaty Field and the treaty signed where the plaza now stands, the Great Bell cast from all four peoples' metal, and the crown's role as keeper of the treaty. New with "The Lands Around Selsior": the Tree Gate and the Bridge Gate, the river running from north to south past the city's west side, the World Tree Road's three stretches, the Selsior Downs, the Long Reach, the Upstream Quarries, and the Old Drains over the first city's buried foundations. Still open: how monarchs are chosen; whether the golems of the quarries are new creatures or slept in the stone all along; why the monster changes come in waves; and what drove the Delver up.

docs.title: Urbanograd
docs.text:
The Town of Societal Rebels

Urbanograd is a city unlike any other on Veligor. It was founded 100 years ago, long after the four peoples had united, so its identity has nothing to do with the old wars. It grew up inside the kingdom, built by people who wanted to live their own way: free to express themselves and free of the expectations of ordinary society. Over the century since, it has grown a counterculture all its own.

docs.title: A Kingdom That Had Settled Down
docs.text:
A century ago, Wonder Kingdom had known peace for so long that peace had grown comfortable, and comfort had grown habits. In Selsior, the old guilds decided who could practice which trade, who could sell in which square and which songs could be sung in the theatres. Families expected their children to follow the trade they were born into. Even Kaldemor, for all its warmth, had firm ideas about what a good, honest life looked like.

None of this was cruel. It was simply how things had always been done, and most people were happy with it. But a restless few were not: painters whose work the galleries called vulgar, musicians who played too loud and too fast, tinkerers whose inventions no guild would license, young people who wanted to dress, love and live in ways their elders did not understand. In the capital, they gathered in cellars, rooftops and back-alley taverns, and they began to talk about leaving.

docs.title: The Long Walk
docs.text:
The spark was a small thing. When the theatre guild of Selsior banned a play by Juna Marrow, a young playwright whose comedy poked fun at the city's grandees, she performed it anyway, on a cart in the middle of the market square, to the biggest crowd the square had seen in years. The guild had her cart hauled away. That night, she told her friends she was done asking permission, and that she meant to build a town where nobody would ever have to.

A few weeks later, about three hundred people walked out of Selsior's gates together: artists, musicians, craftspeople without a guild, inventors, wanderers, and plenty who simply wanted something different. Others joined them along the road from Kaldemor, the harbours and the highlands. They called themselves the Walkers, and the day they left is still celebrated in Urbanograd as Walkout Day.

docs.title: The Empty City
docs.text:
The Walkers did not build Urbanograd from nothing. They settled in Old Grad, in the west of the island: the ruins of a walled stronghold built by the Aristocrats in the Age of Division and abandoned after the founding of the kingdom, when nobody needed fortresses anymore. For generations it had stood empty: crumbling towers, roofless halls and a maze of narrow streets slowly being taken back by weeds.

The Walkers saw something else in it. They patched the roofs with whatever they could find, strung lanterns between the towers, painted every bare wall and turned the old barracks into workshops, theatres and homes. They added the name the city still carries: Urbanograd, roughly "the city of Grad", half a joke about the grand old fortress and half a promise of what it would become.

The first winters were hard. The Walkers knew a great deal about art and very little about farming, and more than one of them went home. Those who stayed learned to trade their crafts, music and inventions for food, and travelers began to come just to see the strange new town.

docs.title: The Kingdom's Answer
docs.text:
Not everyone was pleased. Some in Selsior called the Walkers deserters, and a few guild masters asked the crown to send them home. The question went all the way to the royal court.

The answer came from the founding treaty itself. It promised that every people of Veligor could live together in peace, whatever their culture. The court ruled that the promise did not only protect the four peoples who had signed it, but any people who chose to live differently, so long as they kept the kingdom's peace and laws. Urbanograd was recognized as a town of Wonder Kingdom, with the same rights as any other.

That ruling, known in Urbanograd as the Open Charter, is the reason the city exists as it does today. Its people have never forgotten that the kingdom chose to welcome them, and that is why their rebellion has always been about how they live, never about overturning the realm that let them.

docs.title: A Century of Urbanograd
docs.text:
Over the next hundred years, Old Grad filled up. Each generation built on top of the last, so the city grew upward rather than outward: houses stacked on houses, bridges between rooftops, staircases that lead to three different places at once. New arrivals kept coming from every town on Veligor, bringing their own crafts and ideas and making the city ever more varied.

Today Urbanograd is a busy, noisy, colorful town, famous for its music, its street art, its workshops and its night markets. Juna Marrow's play is performed in the main square every Walkout Day, on a cart, as it was the first time.

docs.title: Cultural Identity
docs.text:
Urbanograd is famous as the home of societal rebels. Its people prize individuality, creativity, unconventional thinking, free expression and the right to live differently. The city draws anyone who loves alternative lifestyles and unusual art, music and fashion.

The city has no lord or chieftain. Matters that concern everyone are talked out at the Open Table, a long gathering in the old fortress's great hall where anyone who lives in Urbanograd may speak. It is loud, slow and often funny, and its people would not have it any other way.

But its people are not revolutionaries. They have no wish to unsettle the kingdom, topple its institutions or quarrel with their neighbors. Their rebellion is cultural and personal, not political.

docs.title: Relationship with Wonder Kingdom
docs.text:
Urbanograd is a full and proud part of Wonder Kingdom. Its people respect the kingdom and get along well with every other community, and the rest of Veligor accepts the city's unusual character. Its people are understood, not distrusted. Even Selsior's guilds, which once wanted the Walkers brought home, now send their apprentices to Urbanograd to see what new things its workshops have come up with.

Urbanograd shows that the kingdom's founding promise reaches further than peace between the original four peoples. Wonder Kingdom also welcomes communities that invent entirely new ways of living.

docs.title: The Lands Around Urbanograd
docs.text: Old Grad stands on its rise in the west of Veligor, and the city has only one way out: the old fortress gate at the end of the Gate Walk. Three roads leave from below it. The royal road runs east across the island to Selsior. Stonefang Pass climbs northeast into the red rock toward Midbarium. The Western Merchant Road, the Aristocrats' old road to the sea, runs southwest to Goa Harbour and is described on that town's page. Inside the walls there is nothing to fear. Outside them, the Gate Watch keeps count: Brindle chalks every sighting on the slate by the gate, and the numbers only go one way.

docs.title: The Gate Meadows
docs.text: All three roads begin in the same place: the open meadows below the gate, where Patch learned her herbs as a girl and carts pull up to wait for morning. A city that keeps building upward needs somewhere to keep its timber and stone, so half the meadows are stackyards: piles of beams and fortress stone, half-built scaffolds, rope cranes and sheds, all of it painted by somebody at some point. Creatures have learned to den among the stacks. Adders sun themselves on the warm stone, and the low, shining-eyed things Dagny sees from the gate at night come up out of the old ditches to hunt among the timber. The way into the Outworks opens from the meadows, where the old ditches run off along the foot of the walls.

docs.title: The Walkers' Road
docs.text: The royal road from Selsior is the way the Walkers came, a century ago, with their bundles and their cart, and Urbanograd has called it the Walkers' Road ever since. From the Gate Meadows it runs east past the edge of the Bristlewood to the Halfway Stone, a tall grey marker that the Walkers are said to have slept beside on their first night out of Selsior's sight. Urbanograd's builders keep a stone depot there, with a crane, a scaffold and a carters' shelter, and the crossroads is busy by day and noisy with creatures by night: rats in the stone stacks, things with too many arms in the drainage pools, adders in the verge. Beyond the stone the road runs on toward the central plain and the capital. Since the year after Rook's first letter to the queen, the Royal Guard's road patrols have ridden its whole length, all the way to the Gate Meadows.

docs.title: Stonefang Pass
docs.text: Stonefang Pass is the highland road. Wool carters bring it down from the hills, and Torvi came down it six years ago meaning to stay a week. From the Gate Meadows it bears northeast into the Seepwater Foothills, where springs seep out of the rock and turn the low ground to bog: reed beds, rotten boardwalks, mist in the mornings, and lumpish bog-lurchers that heave themselves out of the pools at anyone who leaves the planks. Beyond the foothills the pass climbs out of the wet into the Western Descent, a road of red rock ledges and switchbacks where dark, walking stumps root along the path and the axe-headed kind wait at the turns. At the top of the descent stand the needle-sharp spires that give the pass its name, and beyond them the pass comes out on Midbarium's western edge, where the highland families' own country begins.

docs.title: The Outworks
docs.text:
The Aristocrats did not trust walls alone. Around the foot of Old Grad they dug ditches, raised earth banks and built small outer towers, and when they left, all of it fell into ruin. Urbanograd calls this ring of tumbled stone, brambles and half-buried cellars the Outworks. It is reached from the Gate Meadows and runs right round the city's outward side.

For a hundred years the Outworks were a place for children's dares. This year they are where the trouble at the walls comes from. Lux finds outer lanterns smashed in the mornings, never on the same night twice. Dagny sees pairs of eyes low in the brush beyond the road. Both are true, and they are two different things. The eyes belong to gloomeyes, lizard-like creatures with great shining eyes that have crept out of the old ditches to hunt along the walls. The lanterns are the work of lampbats, a swarm that roosts in the flooded cellars under the ruin of the outermost tower, which Urbanograd calls the Fallen Tower, and that throws itself at any light on the walls.

The swarm has a leader. The Gloamwing is a bat the size of a market awning, Disturbance-touched, that hunts every second night and drives the swarm before it. It hates noise, and that is what Drum half-noticed without being able to prove it: on nights the beat in Lantern Square is loudest, the lanterns survive.

The story of the Outworks begins with Brindle, who needs someone to stand the night watch beside Dagny and find out what the eyes are. It runs through Lux's watch on the outer walls and a crate of new panes carried from Tinsel's furnace before the lanterns go dark, a basket of herbs for Patch from the meadows inside the old ditches, and Drum's rhythm, played for the first time outside the gate, to scatter the swarm. It ends under the Fallen Tower, with the Gloamwing. At the far, eastern end of the Outworks, the ditches give out among trees: the edge of the Bristlewood.

docs.title: The Bristlewood
docs.text:
East of the city, along the Walkers' Road from within sight of the city's towers almost to the Halfway Stone, lie the wooded hills of the Bristlewood: old oak and hazel, steep stream valleys and boar wallows. The road's travelers have always heard boar in it. Now the boar come out of it, in herds, and charge the carts.

Shade knows the Bristlewood's near edge well, and two of the routes Shade no longer trusts are there: the Silent Cutting, a wooded cutting where the birds have stopped singing, and the Tusk Path, a hill path where the tracks have grown too large. Deeper in, the streams spread into the Reedwater Bottoms, a marshy valley floor of reeds and black pools where the boar wallow and reed-lurkers lie in wait. At the edge of the bottoms, two days out from the city by cart, is the stream bank where Zip chased something large and tusked, fell, and broke her arm in two places last spring. At the top of that bank Torvi found tracks bigger than any boar's. Zip has named it Zip's Bank, and has asked everyone else to call it that too.

The tracks belong to Hackleback, a boar heavier than a loaded wagon, so deeply touched by the Disturbance that its bristles have gone hard as iron. It has made its home in the Wallow, a deep mud hollow at the heart of the bottoms, and it drives the lesser boar out of the trees and toward the road ahead of it.

This is the hunt that Hatch can no longer make alone. His story is a teacher's: first a test of whether the hero can read tracks at the wood's edge, then Shade's new route past the Tusk Path, then Hatch's own notes, recovered from the camp he had to abandon in the Bristlewood when his knees failed him there. Torvi goes back with the hero to Zip's Bank. Zip and Margo's spark lamp get their trial against real boar, and Zip brings the lamp back, as promised. Patch's rarest root, the one she cannot get anywhere else, is found in the Silent Cutting. Last comes the Wallow, and a hunt Hatch plans but cannot walk. Afterwards, Tick writes the fourth version of Zip's story, the first one that is true.

docs.title: The Beacon Downs
docs.text:
Beyond the Bristlewood's far end the trees thin and the land climbs onto high, bare chalk downs that roll away east toward the middle of the island. Along their crest stands a chain of ruined towers: the beacon towers the Aristocrats built to pass fire signals between their strongholds in the Age of Division. Urbanograd calls the whole country the Beacon Downs, and the tallest tower, on the highest hill, the Highbeacon.

The downs are the wild country Perch's pigeons refuse to cross. At dusk the sky above them belongs to the duskhawks, great hook-beaked hunters that strike anything on the wing, and the grass below belongs to grey downs wolves and to rams with horns like millstones. The routes the pigeons will not fly at any hour pass over the Highbeacon itself, where Stormcrest nests: a raptor with a wingspan wider than a city street, deeply touched by the Disturbance, that has taken the old tower for its eyrie.

The Beacon Downs are also the nearest high ground from which to look east toward the middle of the island, and that brings in Starling. The story of the downs begins in Perch's loft, with a message the birds refuse to carry, which the hero walks over the downs on foot and gives to a bird released on the far side. It goes on through the dusk skies and the duskhawks, a new lens carried from Tinsel's furnace to Starling's roof through the evening crowds, and long nights on the downs. On one of them, from the ruins of a lower beacon, Starling and the hero watch the far horizon waver, just as Starling has seen it from the Rooftops, and find that it wavers far beyond the downs, further east than anyone can walk in a night. It is not the downs' doing. But on the nights it comes, the duskhawks are restless and hunt late, and that is why some of Starling's dates match Perch's list and some do not.

The story ends at the Highbeacon with Stormcrest. Afterwards, the pigeons fly the dusk routes again, though not every route. The hero carries Starling's dates and Perch's list to Rook, who reads them twice, says nothing funny at all, and sends them to Queen Aveline in the next letter. What the flicker is, nobody in Urbanograd can say.

docs.title: Low Grad
docs.text:
Old Grad was built as a fortress, and fortresses go down as well as up. Under the Great Hall, behind the kitchens, is an iron door that the Walkers found locked a century ago and never had a key for. Below it lie the old fortress's buried levels: the halls of the old keep, storerooms and vaults, flooded cisterns, the sally tunnels the garrison used to leave the fortress unseen, and the quarry the Aristocrats cut Old Grad's dark stone from. The city calls all of it Low Grad, and until this summer nobody had been down.

It begins with Velvet's warm stone, and with Tick's notebook. Velvet bought the stone from a frightened wanderer off the deep roads. In his notebook, Tick has written down that same wanderer's story: he sheltered from a storm in a tunnel mouth in the hills, followed it a long way underground, and came out running, with a dark stone in his pocket that would not cool. Brindle hears the story and sees what it might mean: tunnels under the country that may run all the way to the fortress, and a way into the city that no gate guards. The Open Table argues the question for a whole night (Bastian argues both sides, and wins both), and then agrees to open the door. Hex, who learned locks before boxes, opens it, delighted by its Aristocrat lock.

Low Grad goes down in four levels. The Undercroft holds the old keep's halls and the Aristocrats' storerooms, full of rot, dust and creeping slimes. The Floodwells are flooded halls where lurkers lie in the dark water. The Deep Roads are the sally tunnels, long and narrow, roosted by bats and running out under the hills toward the wanderer's tunnel mouth. Last comes the Warm Quarry, where the dark stone is warm to the touch and creatures of that same stone have stirred. The quarry's master is the Warmstone Colossus, a giant of dark stone and the deepest-touched thing beneath the city.

The keeper of Low Grad is Leland, an old well-digger who knows more about what lies under the city's streets than anyone alive, and whom the Table has named Keeper of the Low Door. He keeps the door, the ropes and a chalk map of every level that grows a little each day, and he lets anyone with the nerve go down, as often as they like. At the end of the Deep Roads, the Watch has set an iron grate from Ferro's forge across the tunnel. A chip of the warm stone sits on Tinsel's windowsill with the other failed experiments, and it is still warm.

docs.title: Leadership Today
docs.text: Urbanograd still has no lord. Each year the Open Table chooses a Caller to convene it and keep order, and the Caller rules no one. This year's Caller, for the first time, is Rook, a chandler from Workshops Row whose great-grandparent was one of the Walkers. The Table chose Rook this spring because Rook hates making speeches and loves listening to them. Rook has also written to Queen Aveline every fortnight for nine years.

Design notes

The atmosphere is inspired by MapleStory's Kerning City. Juna Marrow, the Walkers, Old Grad, the Open Charter and the Open Table are new with this page. Urbanograd lies in the west of the island, as the game's world map has it. Still open: what the city looks like beyond its fortress core.

The Lands Around Urbanograd are new with this section: the Gate Meadows and their stackyards, the Walkers' Road and the Halfway Stone, Stonefang Pass's Seepwater Foothills and Western Descent (the spires and the far canyon bridge belong to Midbarium's side), the Outworks, the Bristlewood, the Beacon Downs, Low Grad, their creatures and bosses, and Leland. Still open: what the horizon flicker is; why the stone of the Warm Quarry is warm, and whether Velvet's stone is the same; and what the wanderer saw underground. None of them is tied to the Balrog here. The bosses are Disturbance-touched creatures, nothing more. The Walkers' Road follows the Long Walk in spirit; exactly which way the Walkers went is not recorded.

docs.title: Elite and Epic monsters
docs.text:
Each defeat raises the chance that the next monster to appear is Elite by 1.5% (up to 30%). After 3 elites, an Epic monster appears.

Elite Epic Modifiers 1 2 HP multiplier x8 x30 EXP multiplier x6 x25 Touch multiplier x2 x3 Attack multiplier x2 x3 Defense multiplier x2 x3 Extra drop rolls 1 2 Meso multiplier x3 x8

Modifiers an elite can roll:

  • Elemental: one of fire, ice, lightning, poison
  • Shielded: a shield of 40% of its HP that refills after 5 s without being hit
  • Regenerating: heals 2% of its HP per second after 3 s without being hit
  • Shockwave: a ground slam for 150% damage every 5 s
  • Swift: moves at 140% speed

  • Hale's Bounty (gives)

Dialogue
  • I look after the park gate and the meadow beyond it. What can I do for you, Player?
    • Choice: What is out in the meadow?
    • Choice: Any advice for a newcomer?
    • Choice: Take me to the Snail King's hollow.
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Mostly snails: green ones near the town, blue ones and red ones a little farther. They are slow and harmless enough, but they nibble.
  • East of the town square, past the portal, the meadow opens up. Hunt a few and you will learn how a fight goes.
  • Press Ctrl to swing, and keep a potion on a key. Whatever the snails leave behind, Z picks it up.
  • Then keep your potions close and your feet moving, Player. Jump the red marks, and do not stay still when it sweeps. I will open the way.
  • Walk safe, Player.

docs.title: Lia
docs.text:
Town Guide

Where Kaldemor Services Quests

Welcome to Kaldemor, Player!

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "New in town? Ask me anything!"
  • "Press Space near someone to talk to them."
  • "The market is just east of here."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Welcome Home (gives)
Dialogue
  • Hi, Player! I show newcomers around Kaldemor. Ask me anything!
    • Choice: Where am I?
    • Choice: What is there to do here?
    • Choice: Anything new in town?
    • Choice: Am I ready for the fields?
    • Choice: How do I...?
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Of course! What would you like to know?
    • Choice: ...move and fight?
    • Choice: ...see how strong I am?
    • Choice: ...learn and use skills?
    • Choice: ...carry and wear things?
    • Choice: ...keep track of my quests?
    • Choice: Never mind.
  • Walk with the arrow keys and jump with Alt. Up takes a portal or climbs a ladder, and Down with Alt drops through a ledge.
  • Swing with Ctrl, pick up what monsters leave behind with Z, and talk to people with Space or a click. Every key can be changed with the backslash key.
  • Press S to open your stat window: your level, HP and MP, and the strength, dexterity and the rest that decide how hard you hit.
  • Every level gives you ability points to spend there. A warrior puts most of them into STR.
  • Press K for your skills. Each level from the second one gives you skill points, and a click on the + puts one into a skill.
  • A skill has a key of its own, and costs MP each time you use it. Blue potions bring the MP back.
  • Press I for your inventory: four tabs, one for what you wear, drink, collect and sit on. Double-click a potion to drink it.
  • Press E for what you wear: double-click a piece of equipment to put it on, and a worn one to take it off.
  • Press Q for your quest log: what you can take up, what you are doing, and what you have done. Pick a quest to read its story and its rewards.
  • The quests you follow are listed on the right of the screen with how far you are. Click one to open it in the log.
  • This is the town square of Kaldemor. The big treehouse behind us is the oldest building in town.
  • The people here are friendly. Say hello to everyone: press Space near someone, or click them!
  • Visit the Market to the east for potions and gear. When you feel strong, the fields beyond the town are full of monsters to practice on.
  • People with a light bulb over their head have a job for you. Helping them is a good way to learn your way around!
  • Oh, yes! The clock tower in the park has stopped. Nobody can say when it will tick again.
  • Old Ewan, the clockkeeper, has been up there for days. Maybe he would like some company.
  • You carry (how many you carry) Red Potions - good. Snails nibble, and a potion mends it. Drink one with its key before it gets serious!
  • I would take some Red Potions along first: you carry (how many you carry). Bram sells them in the market, east of here.
  • Have fun, Player!

docs.title: Perrin
docs.text:
Royal Courier

Where Selsior

No time to talk, Player. Letters wait for no one.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Letters for Midbraium, letters for the harbours, and one for the World Tree."
  • "Out of my way! Official business."
  • "Fastest courier in the kingdom, and I have the blisters to prove it."

docs.title: Pim
docs.text:
Recruit

Where Knights' Court

Recruit Pim, reporting! Er... at ease, Player?

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Again! One more round of drills!"
  • "Captain Rhys says my guard is full of holes."

docs.title: Quill
docs.text:
Drillmaster

Where Kaldemor Park Services Run: Kaldemor Gauntlet

Chin up, Player. Eyes front.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Footwork wins more fights than muscle."
  • "Again! Once more, from the top!"
  • "A course does not care how brave you feel."
Dialogue
  • I drill those who want to be tested, Player. Spikes, rocks, platforms that will not wait for you, and a yard full of things that bite. What will it be?
    • Choice: What is the Gauntlet?
    • Choice: I want to run the Kaldemor Gauntlet.
    • Choice: I want to run the Kaldemor Gauntlet.
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Three stages, one after the other. First the yard: whatever I turn loose, you beat down. Then the hanging course: gather the star shards and reach the far ledge before the clock runs out. Then the last stand: hold out for a full minute.
  • Fall, flee or run out of time, and it is over. Come back and I will send you in again, no waiting. Potions are allowed. Scrolls are not.
  • Not yet, Player. Come back at level 10 and I will put you through it.
  • Good. Keep your potions close and your feet moving, Player. In you go.
  • Walk tall, Player.

docs.title: Rhys
docs.text:
Captain of the Royal Guard

Where Knights' Court Services Quests

Stand tall, Player.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "A sword is only as good as the arm behind it."
  • "The Guard trains its next Swordsmen here."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• The Swordsman's Trial (gives)
  • The Swordmaster's Trial (gives)
  • The Grand Swordmaster's Trial (gives)
  • The Sword Saint's Trial (gives)
Dialogue
  • I am Captain Rhys. I train warriors of the Royal Guard in the Swordsman's way.
    • Choice: What is a Swordsman?
    • Choice: Can I advance?
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • A Warrior who has learned patience. The Swordsman fights with fast, controlled cuts, where other Warriors only swing hard.
  • It is the first step on the Swordmaster's road, the one a Warrior takes from level 30. The road goes on: the Swordmaster from level 70, the Grand Swordmaster from level 120, and last the Sword Saint from level 160.
  • Not yet, Player. Come back at level 30, and we shall see whether you are ready for the Guard's trial.
  • You have the strength for it, Player. Speak to me again and I will set you the Guard's trial.
  • You are one of us already, Player, and the road goes on: the Swordmaster. Come back at level 70, and the Guard will set you its next trial.
  • Level seventy, Player. Speak to me again and I will set you the Swordmaster's trial.
  • A Swordmaster, and a fine one. There is one step more, the Grand Swordmaster. Come back at level 120.
  • Level one hundred and twenty, Player. Speak to me again and I will set you the last trial.
  • A Grand Swordmaster stands at the top of the Guard, Player, yet the old books name one rank more, the Sword Saint. Come back at level 160.
  • Level one hundred and sixty, Player. Speak to me again and I will set you the old test, the Sword Saint's.
  • There is no rank above yours that I can give, Player. What the sword can teach you now, it teaches on the road.
  • Keep your guard up.

docs.title: Rosa
docs.text:
Baker

Where Kaldemor Market Services Quests

Fresh bread, Player! Mind the steam.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Warm loaves, straight from the oven!"
  • "A little flour never hurt anyone."
  • "Nothing beats bread on a rainy day."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Rosa's Recipe (gives)
  • A Loaf for Bram (gives)
  • A Pot for Rosa (gives)
Dialogue
  • Ah, Player, the one who found my spores! Come in, come in, wipe your boots.
  • Player! I saved you the heel of the loaf, it is the best part. Sit a moment, the oven is warm.
  • My dear Player, there you are. The bakery is as much yours as mine, you know. Take what you like.
  • Welcome to my bakery, Player! What can I do for you?
    • Choice: What do you bake?
    • Choice: Is business good?
    • Choice: Tell me about your oven.
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Bread, mostly: round loaves, long loaves, and my mushroom bread, which the whole town swears by. The terrace oven has not gone cold in years.
  • The secret is in the spores. Do not tell anyone I said so.
  • Oh, it is lively! Half the market comes up my steps before noon, and the other half comes after.
  • Oh, it is lively! And half of them ask after you, Player. You have a name in Kaldemor now, did you know? The mayor's own bread comes from this oven.
  • You want the oven's story? My grandmother built it with her own hands, brick by brick, the year the clock tower was raised. She said a bakery without a warm oven is only a shop.
  • I have never told that to a customer. Somehow you do not feel like one anymore, Player.
  • Come back hungry, Player!

docs.title: Says

    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • A cab runs between towns with a taxi stand, never into the wilds. You have to have walked to a town before I will drive you there.

docs.title: Tobe
docs.text:
Recruit

Where Knights' Court

I read about swordsmanship. The book did not mention how heavy swords are.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:

  • "The manual says the third cut is the hard one."

docs.title: Tobin
docs.text:
Mayor of Kaldemor

Where Kaldemor Services Quests

Welcome to Kaldemor, Player!

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Lovely weather today."
  • "Have you met Lia, our guide?"
  • "That treehouse has outlived three mayors, and I am the third."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Welcome Home (completes)
  • Settling In (gives)
  • Snail Trouble (gives)
  • Shells for the Mayor (completes)
  • Strength of a Warrior (gives)
Dialogue
  • Ah, Player! Lia told you about the clock tower, did she? Old Ewan has been fretting about it for days.
  • Welcome to Kaldemor, the greenest town this side of the old forest. What can I do for you?
    • Choice: Tell me about Kaldemor.
    • Choice: Who are you?
    • Choice: Guess how many people live here.
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Kaldemor grew up around the great treehouse behind me. The mushroom houses came later - the soil here grows them big enough to live in!
  • West of the square is the Park, with the clock tower and the old windmill farm. East is the Market: potions, weapons, bread, all of it.
  • Walk through the glowing portals with the up arrow to go between them.
  • I'm Tobin, mayor of this town for thirty years now. Would you like to hear how Kaldemor began?
  • Long ago a traveller planted a single seed in this meadow and slept under it for a night. In the morning it was a tree taller than a tower.
  • People came to see it, and some never left. That traveller's name is lost, but we still say: every great town starts with one seed.
  • Another time, then. Old men always have time for stories.
  • A guess, is it? Go on: how many people live in Kaldemor, would you say?
  • N, you say? Not bad, Player! There are just under three hundred of us - not counting the snails.
  • Take care out there, Player. Come back any time!

docs.title: Professions
docs.text:
Gathering professions take materials from nodes in the fields; making professions turn them into items.

Professions go up to level 99. Ranks: Novice (1), Apprentice (20), Journeyman (40), Expert (60), Master (80).

docs.title: Story quests
docs.text: Quest Level From Summary Welcome Home 1 Lia Lia says the mayor wants to meet you. Go and see Tobin. Settling In 1 Tobin Tobin wants you to see the Market and meet Bram, the potion seller. Snail Trouble 2 Tobin Snails are eating the town's gardens. Thin them out in the meadow, then see Ranger Hale at the park gate. Shells for the Mayor 2 Hale Mayor Tobin collects snail shells for the new fence. Bring him 15 Green Snail Shells. Strength of a Warrior 3 Tobin Tobin says a warrior is measured by more than errands. Reach level 5 and use Power Strike five times. He will teach you Warrior's Resolve. The Clock Stopped 4 Ewan The clock tower in the park has stopped. Old Ewan thinks a Shroom took its gear: hunt 20 Shrooms, then bring the gear back. The Snail King 12 Hale Ranger Hale has heard something huge in a hollow beyond the woods. Walk to Kaldemor Woods, the forest edge past the hills, and tell him what you find. The Swordsman's Trial 30 Rhys Captain Rhys will take a Warrior of level 30 into the Swordsman's way. Prove it in the Greenwood Clearing on the royal road: defeat 30 of its monsters and bring back 5 trial seals. The Swordmaster's Trial 70 Rhys Captain Rhys will take a Swordsman of level 70 into the Swordmaster's way. Prove it with a long hunt in the Greenwood Clearing on the royal road: defeat 200 of its monsters. The Grand Swordmaster's Trial 120 Rhys Captain Rhys will take a Swordmaster of level 120 to the top of the sword's road. Prove it once more in the Greenwood Clearing: defeat 400 of its monsters. The Sword Saint's Trial 160 Rhys Captain Rhys will take a Grand Swordmaster of level 160 beyond the Guard's ranks, to the Sword Saint. Prove your edge in the Greenwood Clearing: defeat 600 of its monsters.

docs.title: Side quests
docs.text: Quest Level From Summary Rosa's Recipe 3 Rosa Rosa the baker needs 10 Mushroom Spores and 5 Blue Snail Shells for her famous mushroom bread. A Loaf for Bram 3 Rosa Rosa trusts you with something personal: carry her word to Bram, the potion seller in the Market. A Smith's First Bar 3 Gareth Gareth the smith will show you the forge's first lesson: strike 4 copper ore from the veins in the fields, then smelt it into a copper ingot (open the Professions window and make it). A Pot for Rosa 4 Rosa Rosa the baker will teach you the kitchen's first lesson: pick 3 marjoram flowers from the patches in the fields, then toss a herb salad from them (open the Professions window and make it). A Steady Brew 5 Bram Bram the potion seller will show you how a potion is brewed: pick 4 marjoram flowers from the patches in the fields, then brew 2 red potions from them (open the Professions window and make them). A Head for Heights 3 Garrick Garrick the climber will teach Rope Up to anyone who can reach the lookout on the high ledge of Kaldemor Hills by the vine on its west side. A Sharper Sword 3 Gareth Gareth the smith gives you a Scroll for One-Handed Sword for ATT. Use it on a one-handed sword: drag the scroll from the Use tab onto the sword, worn (equipment window) or carried (Equip tab). A sword is on sale in his shop.

docs.title: Repeatable quests
docs.text: Quest Level From Summary Hale's Bounty 3 Hale Ranger Hale pays a bounty for thinning out the meadow: defeat 30 of the field's monsters. He will pay it again, any time.

docs.title: A Head for Heights
docs.text:
Garrick the climber will teach Rope Up to anyone who can reach the lookout on the high ledge of Kaldemor Hills by the vine on its west side.

Category Side Given by Garrick Level 3 After Settling In

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach the hills' lookout in Kaldemor Hills

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 150 EXP
  • Skill: Rope Up
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • You climbed my ladder to get up here, so you have the hands for it. I have a trick that spares you the climb: Rope Up, a leap that throws you onto the rope or ledge above.
  • But I teach only those who have seen the world from above. Climb the long vine on the west side of Kaldemor Hills, as far as the lookout on its high ledge, then come back to me.
  • The hills are west of the town square. The vine is long, and the grass up there is soft if you slip.
  • Heights are not for everyone. The offer stands.
  • The lookout is at the top of the long vine on the west side of Kaldemor Hills, Player. Climb up, look around, then come back.
  • Ha! You have the look of someone who has seen the clouds up close. Right: bend your knees, look up, and let go.
  • That is Rope Up. Open the skills window with K, find it on the Beginner tab and drag it onto a key; Page Down is its key until you move it. It throws you up to the nearest rope or ledge above, so mind the ceilings.

docs.title: A Loaf for Bram
docs.text:
Rosa trusts you with something personal: carry her word to Bram, the potion seller in the Market.

Category Side Given by Rosa Level 3 After Rosa's Recipe Condition standing npc rosa >= Friend

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Talk to Bram

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 200 EXP
  • Orange Potion x5
  • +150 standing with Rosa
  • +15 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Player, you are a friend now, so I may ask you something I would ask no customer. Bram and I quarrelled over a loaf, years ago, and I never mended it.
  • Would you go to Bram, in the Market, and tell him the oven is warm for him? That is all. He will understand.
  • Thank you, dear. Take the portal east of the square, his stall is at the far end of the Market.
  • Of course. It has waited years, it can wait a little more.
  • Bram is at the far end of the Market, Player. Tell him the oven is warm.
  • Rosa said that? The oven is warm, for me? Well, well. Tell her I will come by for a loaf, and that I was the stubborn one.
  • He said he will come? Oh, Player. I could hug you, and I will, as soon as I take this tray out.
  • Here, a few Orange Potions for your trouble. You have given me more than that.

docs.title: A Pot for Rosa
docs.text:
Rosa the baker will teach you the kitchen's first lesson: pick 3 marjoram flowers from the patches in the fields, then toss a herb salad from them (open the Professions window and make it).

Category Side Given by Rosa Level 4 After Rosa's Recipe

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Gather 3 Marjoram Flower
  2. Make 1 Herb Salad

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 150 EXP
  • 150 mesos
  • Recipe: Roast Pork (Cooking)
  • +50 standing with Rosa
  • +10 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • You have been such a help with the spores, Player, that I would like to hand you more than money. A baker is only half a cook! Pick 3 marjoram flowers from the little patches in the fields (press the gather key beside one), then toss a herb salad from them in your Professions window. Do that and I will teach you my roast pork.
  • Marjoram grows where the grass is thick: the east and west fields have plenty. It comes back by itself, so pick without a worry.
  • The pot will keep warm. Come back when you feel hungry for it.
  • Three marjoram flowers from the patches, then a herb salad. Press the gather key beside a patch.
  • A salad made with your own hands! Nothing in the shop tastes like it.
  • Here is your pay, and my roast pork: its recipe is yours now. A pig's head, a little firewood and a sprig of rosemary, and not a minute more on the fire.

Category Side Given by Gareth Level 3 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Use Scroll for One-Handed Sword for ATT 100%

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 60 EXP
  • Scroll for One-Handed Sword for ATT 100% x1
Dialogue
  • A good smith never stops at the first blow, Player. A blade can be sharpened with a scroll: it adds to its attack, and each scroll takes one of the sword's upgrade slots for good. I will give you one for a one-handed sword. Use it on yours, and I will give you a second to keep. If you have no sword, there is one on my shelf.
  • Here is the scroll. Drag it from your Use tab onto the sword, worn or in your bag. Careful: the sword only has so many slots.
  • Another day, then. The scroll will keep.
  • Drag the scroll from your Use tab onto a one-handed sword. If you have none, I sell a plain Sword.
  • There, it bites deeper now. Keep this second scroll for the next sword, and here is something for your trouble.

docs.title: A Smith's First Bar
docs.text:
Gareth the smith will show you the forge's first lesson: strike 4 copper ore from the veins in the fields, then smelt it into a copper ingot (open the Professions window and make it).

Category Side Given by Gareth Level 3 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Gather 4 Copper Ore
  2. Make 1 Copper Ingot

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 120 EXP
  • 200 mesos
  • Recipe: Bronze Axe (Smithing)
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Bring me a bar, Player, and I will teach you more than a shopkeeper ever could. The fields are full of copper veins: stand by one and press the gather key, a few blows and it gives. Strike 4 copper ore, then smelt a copper ingot from it in your Professions window. Do that and I will teach you the bronze axe.
  • Good. The veins glitter in the east and west fields. They fill again after a while, so there is always more.
  • The forge will keep. Come back when your arms itch for it.
  • Four copper ore from the veins, then an ingot from the ore. Press the gather key by a vein.
  • A fine first bar! Copper is soft, but every smith starts there.
  • Here is your pay, and the bronze axe: its recipe is yours now. Bronze takes a little more skill, but you have the hands for it.

docs.title: A Steady Brew
docs.text:
Bram the potion seller will show you how a potion is brewed: pick 4 marjoram flowers from the patches in the fields, then brew 2 red potions from them (open the Professions window and make them).

Category Side Given by Bram Level 5 After A Pot for Rosa

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Gather 4 Marjoram Flower
  2. Make 2 Red Potion

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 180 EXP
  • 200 mesos
  • Recipe: Orange Potion (Alchemy)
  • +15 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Rosa tells me you cook, Player. A brew is only a pot with a better reason. Pick 4 marjoram flowers from the patches in the fields and brew 2 red potions in your Professions window: two flowers and a mushroom spore make one. Do that and I will teach you the orange potion.
  • Marjoram patches dot the east and west fields. Mushroom spores drop from the Shrooms. Do not drink the first batch, mind.
  • No hurry. The cauldron is not going anywhere.
  • Four marjoram flowers, then two red potions: each takes two flowers and a mushroom spore.
  • Two potions, and they do heal. You have the hands for it, Player.
  • Here is your pay, and the orange potion's recipe. It wants lavender, which grows a little deeper in the fields, and the caps of orange mushrooms.

docs.title: The Grand Swordmaster's Trial
docs.text:
Captain Rhys will take a Swordmaster of level 120 to the top of the sword's road. Prove it once more in the Greenwood Clearing: defeat 400 of its monsters.

Category Story Given by Rhys Level 120 Job Swordmaster

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 400 Greenwood monsters (Horny Mushroom, Axe Stump)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 180,000 EXP
  • Advance to Grand Swordmaster

Placeholder

A stand-in until the higher fields exist: it asks for the strongest monsters there are today, the Greenwood Clearing's. Its hunt moves to the region of level 120 when that is built (WORLD M5).

Dialogue
  • Player. Level one hundred and twenty. I have trained a great many Swordmasters in this yard, and few come back to ask for more.
  • The Grand Swordmaster is not a stronger Swordmaster. He is one who no longer waits for the enemy's blow to begin his own, and who can turn it aside while doing so.
  • One last trial, in the place where you began it: defeat 400 of the Greenwood Clearing's Horny Mushrooms and Axe Stumps without once letting your rhythm break.
  • Then go. Four hundred is a lot of cuts, so make each one lead into the next.
  • The last step is the longest. Come back when you are ready for it.
  • Four hundred of the Greenwood's monsters, Player, on the royal road outside the city. Do not let the rhythm break.
  • Four hundred. I watched your cuts from the first to the last, and I could not find the seam between them.
  • Kneel, Player. By the authority of the Royal Guard, I name you a Grand Swordmaster.
  • Blade Tempest, Perfect Counter and Crescent Divide are yours now. Chain them into the Swordmaster's cuts, or fight each by itself: the sword has no wrong way. Use them well.

docs.title: Hale's Bounty
docs.text:
Ranger Hale pays a bounty for thinning out the meadow: defeat 30 of the field's monsters. He will pay it again, any time.

Category Repeatable Given by Hale Level 3 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Field monsters (Snail, Blue Snail, Red Snail)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 100 EXP
  • 200 mesos

The first time you complete it instead: 150 EXP, 300 mesos, +30 standing with Kaldemor

Dialogue
  • The meadow is never empty for long, Player. If you have the stomach, I pay a bounty: 30 monsters of the field, snails of any colour, and I pay it again whenever you bring me another thirty. The first time is a little more.
  • Good. The field is east of the town square. Count them as you go: the tracker does it for you.
  • Another time, then. The snails will wait.
  • Thirty of the field's monsters, Player. Snails of any colour count.
  • Thirty! The meadow can breathe again.
  • Here is your bounty. Come back for another round whenever the snails get bold.

docs.title: Rosa's Recipe
docs.text:
Rosa the baker needs 10 Mushroom Spores and 5 Blue Snail Shells for her famous mushroom bread.

Category Side Given by Rosa Level 3

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 10 Mushroom Spore (taken)
  • Bring 5 Blue Snail Shell (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 250 EXP
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +200 standing with Rosa
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Oh, Player, you look like someone who is not afraid of mushrooms! My famous mushroom bread needs spores and a pinch of ground blue shell, and my usual supplier has gone to visit his sister.
  • Bring me 10 Mushroom Spores from the Shrooms in the woods, and 5 Blue Snail Shells from the blue snails in the meadow. I will pay you in Orange Potions.
  • Wonderful! The Shrooms live in the woods, west of the town square past the hills; the blue snails are in the meadow to the east.
  • No harm done, dear. The oven will keep.
  • You carry (how many you carry) of 10 Mushroom Spores and (how many you carry) of 5 Blue Snail Shells so far. Take your time.
  • Spores and shells, and not a one broken! You are a treasure.
  • Here are your Orange Potions, ten of them. Come by any time, Player, the bread is always warm.

docs.title: Settling In
docs.text:
Tobin wants you to see the Market and meet Bram, the potion seller.

Category Story Given by Tobin Completed with Tobin Level 1 After Welcome Home

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach Kaldemor Market
  • Talk to Bram

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 20 EXP
  • Red Potion x5
  • +10 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • A good traveller knows where to shop. Would you visit the Market, east of the square, and say hello to Bram, the potion seller? Tell him I sent you.
  • Thank you, Player! Take the glowing portal on the east side with the up arrow. Bram's stall is at the far end of the Market.
  • Of course, of course. Come back whenever you like.
  • Have you been to the Market yet? Bram's stall is at the far end. Take the portal east of the square.
  • Oh, Tobin sent you? Welcome, Player! Come back to me whenever you need potions. Tell the mayor that Bram says hello!
  • You met Bram? Splendid! I knew you would fit right in.
  • Please take these Red Potions. They will keep you going out in the fields. Good luck, Player!

docs.title: Shells for the Mayor
docs.text:
Mayor Tobin collects snail shells for the new fence. Bring him 15 Green Snail Shells.

Category Story Given by Hale Completed with Tobin Level 2 After Snail Trouble

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Green Snail Shell (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 120 EXP
  • Wooden Buckler x1
  • +30 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Well done with the snails, Player. Funny thing: the mayor wants their shells to grind into the mortar for the new fence. Would you bring 15 Green Snail Shells to Tobin? They drop from the green snails now and then.
  • Good. Pick up what the snails leave behind with Z, and carry the shells to Tobin in the town square.
  • Fair enough. The shells will keep, and so will I.
  • Fifteen Green Snail Shells for Tobin. You carry (how many you carry) so far.
  • Shells! Splendid, and so many of them. Hale told me you were reliable, Player.
  • Take this Wooden Buckler for your trouble. A fighter needs something to hold in the other hand.

docs.title: Snail Trouble
docs.text:
Snails are eating the town's gardens. Thin them out in the meadow, then see Ranger Hale at the park gate.

Category Story Given by Tobin Completed with Hale Level 2 After Settling In

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 10 Snail

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 60 EXP
  • 100 mesos
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Ah, Player, just the one I wanted! The snails are back in the gardens and eat everything they can reach. Would you thin them out? Defeat 10 Snails in the meadow east of the square, then see Hale, the ranger at the park gate.
  • Thank you, Player! The meadow is through the portal on the east side of the square. Hale will be waiting at the park gate.
  • Another day, then. The snails are not going anywhere. That is rather the problem.
  • Still at it? Ten Snails, in the meadow east of the square. Then Hale at the park gate will see you right.
  • Mayor Tobin said you would come! Ten snails, and the gardens will be quiet for a week.
  • Here is your pay, Player. You have the makings of a fine hunter.

docs.title: Strength of a Warrior
docs.text:
Tobin says a warrior is measured by more than errands. Reach level 5 and use Power Strike five times. He will teach you Warrior's Resolve.

Category Story Given by Tobin Level 3 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach level 5
  • Use Power Strike 5 times

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 200 EXP
  • Bronze Helmet x1
  • Skill: Warrior's Resolve
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Player, I have watched you grow these past days. Snails, shells, errands: not bad for a newcomer. But a warrior is measured by more than errands.
  • Put your points to work. Reach level 5, and learn the Power Strike: open the skill window with K, spend a skill point on it, and use it 5 times on whatever gets in your way.
  • Skill points go into your skills in the K window, and ability points into your stats in the S window. Come back when you have done both, Player.
  • Strength can wait a little. Come back when you feel ready.
  • Level 5 and five Power Strikes, Player. Press K if you have not spent your skill points yet; the strike sits on Shift until you move it.
  • Level 5, and a Power Strike that makes the snails think twice! I knew you had it in you.
  • Take this Bronze Helmet. Keep your head covered and your chin down, and it will serve you well. And take something I cannot wrap: Warrior's Resolve, a battle cry that hardens you for three minutes. It is on the Beginner tab of the skills window; drag it onto a key, or press F1.

docs.title: The Sword Saint's Trial
docs.text:
Captain Rhys will take a Grand Swordmaster of level 160 beyond the Guard's ranks, to the Sword Saint. Prove your edge in the Greenwood Clearing: defeat 600 of its monsters.

Category Story Given by Rhys Level 160 Job Grand Swordmaster

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 600 Greenwood monsters (Horny Mushroom, Axe Stump)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 600,000 EXP
  • Advance to Sword Saint

Placeholder

A stand-in until the fields past level 120 exist: it asks for the strongest monsters there are today, the Greenwood Clearing's. Its hunt moves to the far fields when they are built.

Dialogue
  • Player. Level one hundred and sixty. I have no rank left to give you, and I am told there is one beyond all of them.
  • The old Guard called it the Sword Saint: one for whom the sword is no longer carried but followed, who cuts the sky open and lets a thousand blades answer.
  • I can only set you the old test: defeat 600 of the Greenwood Clearing's Horny Mushrooms and Axe Stumps, and show me that the road has nothing left to teach you.
  • Then go. Six hundred, and each cut leading into the next.
  • Few ask twice. Come back when the sword calls you.
  • Six hundred of the Greenwood's monsters, Player, on the royal road outside the city.
  • Six hundred. I stopped counting the cuts at two hundred and began to watch your blade instead; it no longer seemed to hold you.
  • Kneel, Player, one last time. By the old authority of the Guard, I name you a Sword Saint.
  • Heavenly Severance and Infinite Blade Dance are yours now. Chain them into the cuts you know, as the sword wills. Use them well.

docs.title: The Swordmaster's Trial
docs.text:
Captain Rhys will take a Swordsman of level 70 into the Swordmaster's way. Prove it with a long hunt in the Greenwood Clearing on the royal road: defeat 200 of its monsters.

Category Story Given by Rhys Level 70 Job Swordsman

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 200 Greenwood monsters (Horny Mushroom, Axe Stump)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 40,000 EXP
  • Advance to Swordmaster

Placeholder

A stand-in until the higher fields exist: it asks for the strongest monsters there are today, the Greenwood Clearing's. Its hunt moves to the region of level 70 when that is built (WORLD M5).

Dialogue
  • Player. Level seventy, and still the same steady arm. The Guard has a name for those who get this far: Swordmaster.
  • A Swordmaster does not end a cut. He lets it run into the next, and the next after it. That cannot be taught on a practice dummy, only in a long fight that does not let up.
  • Go back to the Greenwood Clearing, on the royal road outside the city, and defeat 200 of its Horny Mushrooms and Axe Stumps. They are the toughest creatures the Guard can set you against today. Cut them down one after another, and do not stop between cuts.
  • Good. It is a long hunt, so bring potions and patience. Come back when the count is full.
  • A long road needs a steady start. Come back when you are ready.
  • Two hundred of the Greenwood's monsters, Player. The clearing is on the royal road, outside the city. Keep cutting.
  • Two hundred, and your guard never dropped. That is the rhythm I was looking for.
  • Kneel, Player. By the authority of the Royal Guard, I name you a Swordmaster.
  • Four new cuts are yours: Flash Cutter, Blade Cyclone, Thousand Cuts and Rising Blade. Press one while another is still finishing, and it takes over at once. Use them well.

docs.title: The Swordsman's Trial
docs.text:
Captain Rhys will take a Warrior of level 30 into the Swordsman's way. Prove it in the Greenwood Clearing on the royal road: defeat 30 of its monsters and bring back 5 trial seals.

Category Story Given by Rhys Level 30 Job Warrior

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Greenwood monsters (Horny Mushroom, Axe Stump)
  • Deliver 5 Guard's Trial Seal

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,000 EXP
  • Advance to Swordsman
Dialogue
  • Player. Level thirty, and a steady arm. I have been waiting to say this: you are ready for the Guard's trial.
  • A Swordsman does not swing harder. He swings truer. That is learned where the fight is real, not on a practice dummy.
  • Go to the Greenwood Clearing, on the royal road outside the city. Defeat 30 of the Horny Mushrooms and Axe Stumps there, and bring me 5 Guard's Trial Seals. The Guard stamps a seal on a leaf, and those creatures carry them off while you are on trial.
  • Good. Mind the Axe Stumps: they hit harder than they look. Keep your potions close, and come back when it is done.
  • A sword that is not ready is worse than no sword. Come back when you are.
  • Thirty of the Greenwood's monsters and five trial seals, Player. The clearing is on the royal road, outside the city.
  • Five seals, and the clearing quieter for it. I watched for a steady arm, and here it is.
  • Kneel, Player. By the authority of the Royal Guard, I name you a Swordsman.
  • Your cuts will come quicker and truer from now on: the Swordsman's attacks are yours. Use them well.

docs.title: The Clock Stopped
docs.text:
The clock tower in the park has stopped. Old Ewan thinks a Shroom took its gear: hunt 20 Shrooms, then bring the gear back.

Category Story Given by Ewan Level 4 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 20 Shroom
  2. Deliver 1 Clock Gear

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 400 EXP
  • Old Pocket Watch x1
  • +50 standing with Kaldemor
  • Sets kaldemor.clock_running
Dialogue
  • Ah, a visitor! Mind the dust. I am Ewan, keeper of this clock these forty years, and this morning it stopped.
  • The works are not broken. A gear is missing: the great gear, and I would swear a Shroom from the woods dragged it off in the night. They take anything shiny.
  • Thin out 20 Shrooms in the woods, past the hills west of the town square, and bring me my Clock Gear. One of them will have it, I am sure.
  • Thank you, Player. When the Shrooms are fewer, the gear will turn up: bring it straight here. The whole town will thank you when the bell rings again.
  • I understand, it is a long walk. The clock will be here. Not ticking, but here.
  • Twenty Shrooms first, then the gear. The woods are west of the town square, past the hills.
  • My gear! Oh, look at it, not a scratch. Give me a moment...
  • There. Do you hear that? Tick, tick, tick. Kaldemor has its time back.
  • Please take my old pocket watch. It never stopped once in forty years, and I hope it brings you luck.

docs.title: The Snail King
docs.text:
Ranger Hale has heard something huge in a hollow beyond the woods. Walk to Kaldemor Woods, the forest edge past the hills, and tell him what you find.

Category Story Given by Hale Level 12 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach Kaldemor Woods

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 300 EXP
  • +40 standing with Kaldemor
  • Unlocks boss.snail_king
Dialogue
  • You are not the newcomer who carried shells for the mayor any more, Player. So I will tell you what I have not told the others: something huge has settled in a hollow past Kaldemor Woods. The snails do not stray that way now, and the ground shakes at night.
  • I need someone to walk out to Kaldemor Woods, the forest edge beyond the hills, and tell me whether the road to it is clear. If it is, I can show you the way to the hollow myself. Will you go?
  • Good. The woods are west of the town, past the hills. Bring potions, Player: whatever sleeps out there is no snail of the meadow.
  • Wise to be sure of yourself. Come back when you are.
  • Kaldemor Woods, Player: west of the town, past the hills. Walk to it and come back to tell me it is clear.
  • You made it there and back, and you are in one piece. Then it is as I thought: the old giant snail Mano has taken the hollow, and it has called itself a king.
  • Whenever you are ready, ask me and I will take you to the Snail King's hollow. Mind the red marks on the ground: they show where it will land. And remember: no scroll will get you out of there.

docs.title: Welcome Home
docs.text:
Lia says the mayor wants to meet you. Go and see Tobin.

Category Story Given by Lia Completed with Tobin Level 1

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15 EXP
  • +10 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Oh, a new face! Welcome to Kaldemor, Player. Mayor Tobin wants to meet every newcomer. Would you go and see him? He is just west of here.
  • Wonderful! Tobin is the mayor, standing in front of the treehouse. Just walk up to him and talk.
  • No rush. If you change your mind, I am right here.
  • Mayor Tobin is waiting for you, Player. He is just to the west.
  • Ah, you must be Player! Lia told me about you. Welcome to Kaldemor, my dear. I hope you will call it home.
  • Take this as a welcome gift. Come and talk to me again when you are ready for more.

docs.title: Runs
docs.text:
Runs are staged challenges entered through an NPC.

Run Stages Kaldemor Gauntlet 3

docs.title: Kaldemor Gauntlet
docs.text:
Drillmaster Quill's course for those who want to be tested: a yard full of monsters, a course of moving platforms, spikes and falling rocks, and a last stand. Potions work in there; scrolls do not.

Dying ends the run.

docs.title: 1. The Training Yard
docs.text:
Map: The Training Yard

  • Defeat every monster

Wave 1: 3 Pig, 3 Orange Mushroom

Wave 2: 3 Green Mushroom, 2 Stump

Wave 3: 3 Green Mushroom, 2 Stump, 3 Pig

docs.title: 2. The Hanging Course
docs.text:
Map: The Hanging Course. Time limit: 150 s.

  • Collect 3 Star Shards
  • Reach the far ledge

docs.title: 3. The Last Stand
docs.text:
Map: The Last Stand

  • Survive for 60 seconds

Wave 1: 2 Green Mushroom, 1 Pig

docs.title: Rewards (Normal)
docs.text:
First clear: 1,500 EXP, Agent Cape x1, Elixir x2, Unlocks kaldemor.gauntlet_cleared

Every clear: 2,000 mesos, Orange Potion x5, White Potion x3

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
Skill numbers come from formulas of the skill level; each table below works them out level by level.

Skill Group Kind Max level Description Power Strike Warrior Attack 20 A strong strike at one enemy in front. Sweeping Slash Warrior Attack 20 A wide slash that sweeps the enemies in front. Ground Breaker Warrior Attack 20 A heavy double slash at the enemies in front. War Leap Warrior Leap 10 Dash far through the air the way you face: jump again in the air, or press its key. Triple Slash Swordsman Attack 20 Three quick cuts at the enemies in front. Blade Wave Swordsman Projectile 20 Sends a blade of force flying ahead, cutting every enemy in its way once. Counter Slash Swordsman Counter 20 Hold a guard: the first attack or touch that would land on you meanwhile is turned aside, and you strike back hard. With nothing to turn aside it does nothing. Sword Dash Swordsman Dash 20 Dash along the ground, cutting every enemy you pass through once. It stops at a wall or the edge of a ledge. Flash Cutter Swordmaster Attack 20 Two lightning cuts in front, cheap and quick. The start of most chains. Blade Cyclone Swordmaster Attack 20 Spin with the blade out and cut everything around you, over and over. Thousand Cuts Swordmaster Attack 20 A storm of cuts too quick to count, on every enemy in front. Rising Blade Swordmaster Attack 20 Carries you up on a rising cut, hitting everything above you on the way. A good way into the air, and to the next chain. Blade Tempest Grand Swordmaster Attack 30 A burst of blades that sweeps the whole screen around you. Perfect Counter Grand Swordmaster Counter 30 Counter Slash perfected: the first attack or touch that would land on you meanwhile is turned aside, and you answer with a flurry. With nothing to turn aside it does nothing. Crescent Divide Grand Swordmaster Attack 30 A wide crescent cut that splits everything far in front of you. Heavenly Severance Sword Saint Attack 30 A cut from the sky that parts the field in two: everything far in front of you falls to it, wave after wave. Infinite Blade Dance Sword Saint Attack 30 A swarm of blades answers your sword and dances through every enemy near you, again and again. Warrior's Resolve Buff Buff 1 Steel yourself for the fight. docs.title: Status Effects
docs.text:
• Slow: monsters lose 50% of their speed, players 40%
  • Poison, Burning, Bleeding: 5 HP lost every 1 s unless the attack says otherwise
  • Darkness and Weaken: 30% and 30% less damage dealt
  • Curse: 50% less EXP gained
  • Seal: no skills
  • Stun and freeze on a boss last 50% of their time

docs.title: The Hills' Lookout
docs.text:
Region Kaldemor Where Kaldemor Hills Size Common Reward 25 EXP, 100 mesos What you see

From the top of the long vine the whole of the western hills lies below you. Far off in the woods one birch stands taller than the rest, and a squirrel keeps vanishing behind it.

docs.title: Face to Face with the Clock
docs.text:
Region Kaldemor Where Kaldemor Park Size Common Reward 25 EXP What you see

From the climbers' ledge you stand level with the clock tower's face. The hands are stuck, and the gears behind the glass look like they only need a patient hand.

docs.title: The Squirrel's Hollow
docs.text:
Region Kaldemor Where Kaldemor Woods Size Rare Reward 40 EXP, 250 mesos, Red Potion x5 What you see

Behind the woods' birch a hollow in the trunk held a tin box, wrapped in oilcloth, that some traveller hid long ago. The squirrel had been guarding it.

docs.title: The Crossing's Hilltop
docs.text:
Region The Royal Road Where The Crossing Size Common Reward 25 EXP, 150 mesos What you see

From the gazebo's hill both roads show at once: the royal road running west to the capital, and the narrow path that leaves it for the Greenwood.

docs.title: The Greenwood's Crown
docs.text:
Region The Royal Road Where Greenwood Clearing Size Rare Reward 40 EXP, Orange Potion x3 What you see

The crown ledge above the clearing is cut off from the rest by two ladders. Someone has set a log bench here, as if to watch the mushrooms from above.

docs.title: The Skywalk's View
docs.text:
Region Selsior Where Selsior Size Common Reward 25 EXP, 150 mesos What you see

From the skywalk above the plaza the capital spreads out: the Great Bell on its dais, the fountain, and the throne hall's red carpet running up the palace steps.

docs.title: The Great Bell
docs.text:
Region Selsior Where Selsior Size Common Reward 25 EXP What you see

You laid a hand on the Great Bell's rim and it hummed through your arm. The guards say it rings only for coronations, and for no one else.
